newsitem.title: UK: London HK stocks fall after strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: London HK stocks fall after strong U.S. data.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London fell on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected U.S. data sent U.S. Treasury bond prices lower, dealers said.

Figures showed the U.S. economy expanded at a surprising 5.6 per cent annual rate in the first quarter of the year compared to 3.8 per cent for the fourth quarter of last year. Economists had forecast growth of 4.1 per cent.

By 1410 GMT the Hong Kong London Reference index had fallen 136.45 points to 12,766.85. The Hang Seng gained 302.88 points to 12,903.30 earlier in the day after Tuesday's weaker than expected U.S. employment cost and durable goods data propelled a rally on Wall Street.
"We saw the U.S. long bond yield below seven percent yesterday and now it has gone above seven again, shares prices have fallen," said one dealer.
Bucking the downward trend were HSBC Holdings, up 60 cents at HK$ 194.72-1/2, and Hang Seng Bank, which gained 67-1/2 cents to HK$ 86.62-1/2, on selective buying, dealers said.
